items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: Eddie Davis was around there at the time and then he eventually became house band there.

ctx.x: Do you remember the first day you came to the City...how you came and who you were with?
We came in on a bus and I went and stayed at that hotel right next to Minton's,

what is the name of that hotel? Anyway, all the musicians stayed there and anyway I went right into the hotel, then Minton's was right downstairs. And that was just right for me. Boy oh boy, I'd come downstairs every night and Lester Young would be blowin' and Harold ("Doc") West and, oh gee whiz, Don Byas and I got a chance to really hear all these wonderful people and see them in this New York setting, you know what I mean, and it was just wonderful. And of course Kenny Clarke and Monk and, let's see, Eddie…

items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: There was Don Byas and Lester and Dizzy and Eddie Lockjaw Davis, Paul Gonzalves. You can name 'em. All the guys were there all the time.

ctx.x: Well anybody would be subject to be staying there, you know. It's whoever was in town. But, you know, you could eat there...you could eat downstairs, they

had restaurants. And the main thing was that every night there was a jam session. And, if you were off, and naturally you staid upstairs, you come downstairs and you might see anybody there. There was Don Byas and Lester and Dizzy and Eddie Lockjaw Davis, Paul Gonzalves. You can name 'em. All the guys were there all the time. So every night was a different night. It was stimulating.

You were in an interesting position because you came to New York first and worked there for a while, staid in the Cecil Hotel and then, right after that, you went with Tiny Bradshaw back to Chicago, in the Rum Boogie, and I just wonder if anything by way of contrast with the two scenes, at that time Chicago and New York,/struck your attention.
